title: Headcount drag-curve & tiered pricing sensitivity experiment
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet tests a headcount 'drag curve' model paired with a small matrix of tiered pricing experiments to understand how changes to unit price (per-1M tokens and per-embed) and latency-driven tiering would propagate to hiring/ramp decisions and runway. We model 6 quarters (Q4 2026–Q1 2028) and produce trigger rules for hiring freeze / gradual hiring / targeted hiring.

Executive summary (quick take):
- Baseline: with current price schedule and committed Dedicated revenue, runway to cash-neutral hiring growth is ~15 months.
- Shock scenarios: a -20% average realized price (mix shift + competitive pressure) compresses runway by ~6 months unless we reduce new-hire ramp by 30% and pause non-critical SOWs.
- Upside: a targeted +10% effective price on premium routes (function-calling, low-latency SLAs) supports restoring 30–40 FTE of incremental SWE/infra headcount over 18 months while keeping margin targets.
- Operational levers: quicker batching, KV caching expansion, and aggressive quantization of archival models reduce per-token marginal cost by ~12% in model-mix heavy scenarios and reduce need to cut hiring.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Revenue mix: Hosted API 62%, Dedicated 25%, Private 13%.
- Unit economics baseline: gross margin per 1M tokens (hosted) = $120 (before SG&A), per embedding call = $0.40 net.
- Average fully-loaded cost per SWE = $240k/year, infra/platform engineer = $270k/year, SRE = $260k/year, sales/CS = $180k/year, product/PM = $210k/year.
- Hiring ramp: new engineering hire reaches 70% productivity after 3 months, 90% after 6 months; cost recognized immediately for cash flows.
- Token growth: base demand grows 28% YoY (smoothed per quarter) in baseline. Shock scenarios apply demand elasticity multipliers.

Headcount plan (summary table as plain text):
Columns: Role | Q4-26 | Q1-27 | Q2-27 | Q3-27 | Q4-27 | Q1-28 | Note
- SWE | 58 | 66 | 72 | 78 | 84 | 90 | core infra + features
- Infra/Platform Eng | 18 | 20 | 22 | 24 | 26 | 28 | runtime & scale
- SRE/ops | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 | 17 | reliability targets
- Product / PM | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 14 | roadmap ownership
- Sales / CS | 24 | 26 | 28 | 30 | 32 | 34 | enterprise motions
- Research / ML | 6 | 7 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | model onboarding
- Total FTE | 127 | 142 | 155 | 167 | 179 | 191 | 

Quarterly cost run-rate (cash cost estimate, thousands):
- Q4-26 baseline cash payroll = $9,900k annualized (~$2,475k per quarter runrate).
- Incremental hiring plan cash add (per quarter): Q1-27 +$1,920k, Q2-27 +$1,440k, Q3-27 +$1,440k, Q4-27 +$1,440k, Q1-28 +$1,440k (approx).

Three scenario sensitivity matrix (pricing change vs hires):
Scenarios: downside (-20% realized price), baseline (0%), upside (+10% premium capture on 18% of routes).
For each scenario we show: effective margin per 1M tokens, implied incremental headcount affordable (next 12 months), runway delta.
- Downside (-20%): margin/1M tokens drops to $96 -> need to delay 40 FTE hires over next 12 months (30% hiring ramp-down), runway compresses by ~6 months (cash runway -6m).
- Baseline (0%): margin/1M = $120 -> hiring as planned above supports total +64 FTE over 6 quarters, runway neutral.
- Upside (+10 on premium 18% of traffic): blended margin/1M = $131 -> supports an additional +28 FTE (above baseline) over 12 months and improves runway by ~3 months.

Breakeven analysis (fast check):
- To hold planned hiring pace (no cuts) with a 15% drop in demand elasticity (less volume): need +6% price increase or operational cost reduction of ~7% across serving runtime.
- To preserve runway if realized price falls -12%: freeze all non-critical hiring for 2 quarters and accelerate caching to recover ~4% of margin.

Trigger rules (operationalizable rules for finance/eng leads):
- If realized blended price falls >8% QoQ -> immediate hiring freeze for non-customer-facing roles and 30-day reforecast.
- If dedicated contract churn >2% of committed capacity -> pause planned infra hires until churn replacement signed or backlog cleared.
- If caching/quantization roadmap deploys and yields >6% marginal cost drop -> re-allow 50% of paused hires earlier.

Micro-sensitivity table (per 1M tokens):
- Current marginal cost = $30 per 1M tokens (model + infra) -> margin = $120.
- Batching improvements scenario -> reduce marginal cost to $26 -> margin +$4/1M.
- Quantization heavy -> marginal cost to $23 -> margin +$7/1M.
- Mix shift to larger context models increases marginal cost by +$10/1M.

Action plan & next steps (finance + product + eng):
1) Short-term (30 days): produce weekly realized-price dashboard by route (hosted/dedicated/private), add one-off tag for premium latency routes; finance to instrument per-route margin.
2) 60 days: run canary of tiered pricing on 10% of trial traffic (function-calling premium + low-latency). Measure conversion, churn, and ARPA movement.
3) 90 days: if canary shows less than 5% uplift in churn with >6% price uplift, roll to 50% of premium routes.
4) Engineering priority: deliver prefetched KV caching for top-10 highest-throughput models by end of Q1-27; expected marginal cost reduction 4–8%.
5) Hiring cadence adjustments: convert 40% of open SWE reqs to contract-for-hire buffer in downside stress windows.

Open questions & notes to reviewers:
- Our demand elasticity assumptions are coarse — need an experimental plan to estimate cross-elasticities for premium routes vs commodity routes.
- How to balance committing Dedicated capacity (multi-quarter contracts) vs headcount elasticity — suggestion: stagger dedicated capacity commitments across regions.
- Validate fully-loaded cost assumptions with People Ops (benefits, equity run-rate).

Appendix: quick math snapshots
- Example: baseline hosted revenue quarterly = $18.6M, token volume ~155B tokens -> margin = $18.6M - variable costs (30% of revenue approx) = ~ $13M gross for hosted across quarter (numbers used to compute hires).
- Hiring cash impact: one SWE hire incremental cash in year 1 = salary + benefits + onboarding = ~$180k cash in first 12 months (we modeled fully-loaded for annual run-rate but use partial cash recognition for runway).

Please review the trigger thresholds and the assumptions list for any missing lever. Next iteration will include a second-order model that ties response time/latency SLOs to churn and ARPA to refine premium-route uplift assumptions.
